source_refs.note: Topic 9.6 with Example 9.6 (PDF 204-205, printed 201-202). The print's 'energy required' in Example 9.6 is read as energy acquired.

blocks.text: When a particle of charge q moves from point A at potential V_A to a point B at potential V_B keeping electrostatic equilibrium, the change in its potential energy is delta U = q(V_B - V_A) = q delta V ... (9.24). If no external force acts on the charge to maintain equilibrium, this change in potential energy appears as a change in kinetic energy.

Suppose the charge carried by the particle is q = e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C. The energy acquired by the charge is delta K.E. = q delta V = e delta V = (1.6 x 10^-19 C)(delta V). If delta V = 1 volt, delta K.E. = (1.6 x 10^-19 C) x (1 V) = 1.6 x 10^-19 J.

blocks.title: Electron volt
blocks.text: The amount of energy equal to 1.6 x 10^-19 J is called one electron volt, denoted by 1 eV. It is the amount of energy acquired or lost by an electron as it traverses a potential difference of one volt: 1 eV = 1.6 x 10^-19 J ... (9.25).

blocks.title: Example 9.6
blocks.text: A particle carrying a charge of 2e falls through a potential difference of 3.0 V. Calculate the energy acquired by it. Solution: q = 2e, delta V = 3.0 V. delta K.E. = q delta V = (2e)(3.0 V) = 6.0 eV = 6.0 x 1.6 x 10^-19 J = 9.6 x 10^-19 J.
